messages:
maya: Heads up — since the cilium 1.23 rollout in eu-west1 we've been seeing weird east-west tail latency for inference pods. UDP flows show 200–1500ms tails intermittently, and a handful of RDMA sessions failed to handshake. Noticed on ~10% of GPU nodes.
infra-bot: alert: metric udp_retransmit_rate increased 3.8x in cluster eu-west1 between 03:15–03:45 UTC.
sam: Can confirm. Repro with iperf3 UDP between two pods shows packet loss spikes. Sharing quick captures.

sam: tcpdump capture (trimmed) showed a lot of duplicated ACKs and some out-of-order:
```
14:03:21.123456 IP pod-a > pod-b: UDP, length 1200
14:03:21.123789 IP pod-b > pod-a: UDP, length 1200 (dup)
14:03:21.124000 IP pod-a > pod-b: UDP, length 80 (ICMP frag needed?)
```

sam: iperf test: `iperf3 -u -c POD_B_IP -b 800M -t 30` -> jitter spikes to 120ms at ~6s intervals.

jonah: Hmm — this smells like a GSO/GRO or coalescing edge-case with Cilium's CT or encapsulation path. I found kernel dmesg on one node with: `NETDEV WATCHDOG: vxlan0: transmit queue 0 timed out` (paraphrasing).

eli: I also saw an increase in skb->len fragmentation warnings on one node. Could be offload mismatch after the datapath bump.

rachel: Actions: 1) Can we reproduce on a non-GPU node? 2) Workaround to stop tailing while we triage? 3) Rollback window if needed.

maya: Repro'd on a small non-GPU canary, which implies not strictly GPU-driver related. Workaround I tested that helped: turn off GRO on the host veth for a pod pair: `sudo ethtool -K vethXYZ gro off` — that reduced tails in the short test. Not ideal at scale but useful as a mitigation.

jonah: Good find. Another quick mitigation is to disable UDP GRO at the node NIC level if the interface is known: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off` for affected nodes. That avoids kernel coalescing that cilium's bpf path mishandles.

sam: Trying a node-level `gro off` now on 3 nodes in eu-west1-canary. Will post metrics in 10m.

infra-bot: deploybot: rolled back one canary of cilium 1.23 -> 1.22 on k8s-eu-canary-3 as a test (manual).

maya: Preliminary numbers: nodes with GRO off show retransmit rate down ~75% and tail percentiles back to normal. The nodes with cilium rollback are also OK. So both mitigations work short-term.

eli: Filing an issue with Cilium maintainers + attaching tcpdump/trace and kernel logs. Include whether datapath uses direct routing vs encapsulation (we saw both).

rachel: Plan: - Expand GRO off to affected canaries via daemonset patch (runbook step) - Open incident with cilium, include reproduce steps and iperf/tcpdump - Schedule rolling rollback for eu-west1 if we fail to see improvement in 60m - Notify SRE oncall and product owners for impacted customers.

sam: Patch applied to canaries: `kubectl -n kube-system set env daemonset/cilium CILIUM_DISABLE_GRO=true` (we used our wrapper to set ethtool on boot via node-init). Monitoring now.

jonah: Long-term: the datapath change in 1.23 likely added a codepath that doesn't account for skbs with GSO/UDP fragments on our NICs. We'll reproduce in a lab kernel matrix and try to craft a minimal kernel + cilium datapath reproducer. Also check `net.core.rmem_max`/`wmem_max` and UDP buffer tuning as secondary.

maya: Note: RDMA failures were showing as connect timeouts rather than hard errors — suggests the control/UDP channel getting delayed, not immediate packet loss. Keep RDMA test harness running.

rachel: I'll start incident doc + status updates. If anyone sees other clusters showing the same pattern, ping here. :thumbsup:

sam: Update 10m: canary nodes with GRO off -> retransmit metric down 68%, burst tails mostly removed. Proceeding to expand to remaining eu-west1 canaries.

maya: Thanks. Leaving traces and captures in the incident ticket.

jonah: I'll open a PR with a diagnostic daemonset that toggles ethtool flags and collects perf + skb stats for affected pods.

rachel: Good. If rollback is needed we'll use the pre-approved rollback playbook. Will update status channel in 15m.
